small_guidance:
- The conv now dominates (17.8ms vs 10.3ms baseline); the instance_norm kernel is already fine. Marginal tuning gains only — try removing the `x.contiguous()` after conv (it forces an extra NHWC→NCHW copy of 128×128×128×128 fp32 ≈ 1GB) by making the instance_norm kernel stride-aware over channels_last, or by keeping NCHW throughout and skipping channels_last on conv.
- Add autotune configs with smaller BLOCK (1024, 2048) since HW=126*126=15876 — current BLOCK=4096+ wastes lanes via masking on the tail; also try num_warps=4 for this reduction width.
- Fuse the conv bias add into the instance_norm kernel epilogue start (load bias once per (N,C) program) so the post-conv tensor doesn't need a separate bias pass.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with implicit im2col gather. Shapes are N=128, OC=128, OH=OW=126, IC*kh*kw=64*9=576 — a very GEMM-friendly problem. This is where the headroom is; the torch conv is the bottleneck now.
- Fuse the entire pipeline: conv epilogue writes per-(N,C) partial sums for instance-norm statistics into a scratch buffer, then a second kernel does mean/var/normalize/divide. Or, since OH*OW=15876 fits, do a two-pass conv: pass 1 computes conv output + per-(N,C) sum and sum-of-squares in one kernel (atomics or per-tile reduction), pass 2 applies normalize+divide. Eliminates the NHWC↔NCHW round-trip entirely.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) end-to-end: conv writes NHWC, instance-norm reads NHWC with strided access along the spatial-flattened axis but contiguous channel loads — one program per (N, C) still works, just with stride=C between spatial elements.
